Q: Thank you for taking the time to speak with me today. This recorded statement concerns the rear-end collision in
Conroe, Texas. Please sttae your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather just keep it to what happened, if that's okay. I'm the driver who got hit from behind.
Q: That's fine. Can you describe where you were when the collision occurred?
A: I was stopped at a traffic light on the main road, waiting for the signal to change. I had been stopped for myabe ten
or fifteen seconds when I felt the impact.
Q: What did you feel at the moment of impact?
A: A hard jolt from behind. My head snapped back and then forward, and my seatbelt locked up across my chest. I
remember the sound more than anything, a loud bang.
Q: Did you notice any injuries right after the collision?
A: Not right away. I figured I was just shaken up. By that evening my neck was stiff and I had a dull ache running into
my shoulders. The next morning it was worse, and I had trouble turning my head to check my mirrors.
Q: Have you sought medical attention since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to an urgent care clinic first, and then I was referred to a physical therapist. They told me I have
whiplash. I'm still going to appointments and taking anti-inflammatory medication.
Q: Did the other driver stop and exchange information?
A: Yes, they pulled over beihnd me and we exchanged insurance details. They said they were looking down at their
phone when they looked up and realized they were too late to stop.
Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add to your statement?
A: Only that I'm still having headaches and I'm missing some work because sitting for long periods hurts. I'm willing to
provide my medical records.
Q: Thank you. This concludes the recorded statement.
</page>
